description: Generate a seeded synthetic real-symmetric Brownian-matrix path to illustrate eigenvalue repulsion (beta=1). Use for reproducible numerical education or research references; choose spectral_assessment to analyze observed market panels. No market data is accepted or fetched. All arguments are optional: defaults are dimension=6, steps=40, dt=0.05 and seed=0. Returns status=synthetic, parameters, beta, normalization and path with steps+1 snapshots; each snapshot contains synthetic time and ordered eigenvalues, starting from all zeros. Negative eigenvalues are valid because this is not a covariance matrix. There is no mean reversion, market calibration or factor identity tracking. Reuse seed with the recorded runtime and implementation fingerprint for replay. Out-of-range or noninteger size/step/seed inputs return a tool error. Example: {"dimension":3,"steps":5,"dt":0.05,"seed":7}.

dimension.description: Size N of the synthetic real-symmetric N-by-N matrix and number of eigenvalues per step; default 6.

dt.description: Synthetic time increment; default 0.05. This is not seconds or a market horizon. Off-diagonal increment variance is dt/N; diagonal variance is 2*dt/N.

seed.description: Integer random seed for deterministic replay in a recorded Python runtime; default 0. Record the implementation fingerprint and runtime with results.

steps.description: Number of Brownian increments; default 40. The returned path contains steps + 1 snapshots, including the initial zero matrix.
